sanskrit_verse: विकृष्यमाणे क्षेत्रे चेत् क्षेत्रिकः पुनराव्रजेत् । खिलोपचारं तत्सर्वं दत्त्वा स्वक्षेत्रमाप्नुयात् ॥
transliteration: vikṛṣyamāṇe kṣetre cet kṣetrikaḥ punar āvrajet | khilopacāraṃ tat sarvaṃ dattvā svakṣetram āpnuyāt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: If a field is being cultivated by another and the owner returns, the cultivator must yield the entire produce after deducting the cost of cultivation, thereby restoring ownership without conflict.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority rests inherently in the original owner
Causation arises through active engagement with property
Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of prior rights
Restoration logic demands return of benefit minus effort expended
Consciousness alignment requires harmonizing possession with rightful ownership
executable_legal_axioms: IF land is under cultivation AND the original owner reasserts claim THEN cultivator transfers produce balance AFTER subtracting cultivation costs
IF ownership is latent during use THEN user holds temporary custodial capacity UNTIL owner reclaims
IF no dispute exists regarding cultivation effort THEN deduction is standardized to regional average input value
supreme_court_application: In property disputes where interim cultivation occurred, the court shall recognize latent ownership while mandating restitution based on net agricultural gain, ensuring neither party profits unjustly nor suffers loss due to delayed assertion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Ownership manifests through pramāṇa of title; cultivation is anupūrvaśaḥ arising from absence of contest. Responsibility aligns proportionally to labor invested. No punitive measure applies—only completion of transactional integrity restores dharma.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Inventory assessment of crop yield at time of reclaim
Standardized valuation of cultivation inputs applied regionally
Transfer protocol executed within seven days of judgment
Reintegration ceremony acknowledging both parties' roles in dharmic order
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, rightful ownership is restored through conscious completion, not punishment. Dharma prevails when action realigns with inherent truth. Consciousness remains the ultimate adjudicator.
